title: Final twisted-arrow resolution of a cartesian fibration with terminal fibres
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and let $p:R\to N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a cartesian fibration of quasicategories in a containing universe. Suppose that each fibre $R_a$ has a terminal object $t_a$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_{R_a}(r,t_a)$ is contractible for every $r\in R_a$. No transport-preservation assumption on these terminal objects is made. For $u:a\to b$ in $A$, write $u^*:R_a\to R_b$ for cartesian transport along $u^{\mathrm{op}}:b\to a$ in $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Define $K_A=N(\operatorname{Tw}(A)^{\mathrm{op}})$ as follows: its objects are arrows $u:a\to b$ of $A$, and an arrow $u\to u'$ is a pair $f:a\to a'$, $g:b'\to b$ with $u=gu'f$. There is a coherent functor $k:K_A\to R$ over the projection $u:a\to b\mapsto b$ to $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $k(u)\simeq u^*t_a$. On the arrow $(f,g)$ its component is the composite
$$u^*t_a\simeq g^*u'^*f^*t_a\longrightarrow g^*u'^*t_{a'}\longrightarrow u'^*t_{a'},$$
where the middle map is induced by the map to the terminal object $t_{a'}$ and the last arrow is cartesian over $g^{\mathrm{op}}$. The compatible terminal-object and cartesian-lift choices can be made coherently, and any two such constructions are naturally equivalent over $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

This functor $k$ is final in the following strong sense. For every quasicategory $D$ in any further containing universe, coherent diagram $V:R\to D$ and $d\in D$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)}(V,\Delta_Rd)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_A,D)}(Vk,\Delta_{K_A}d),$$
natural in $V,d$. Consequently a specified cocone on $V$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $k$ is colimiting; existence of either colimit implies existence of the other with that cocone. The total $R$ and its mapping spaces need not be small in the universe in which $A$ is small.

source.place: Agent terminal-fibre generalization of the twisted-diagonal contraction in Section 5.6, Proposition 5.6.9, pp. 241-242. The statement here is for a given cartesian fibration, not a classification theorem; see report.md for the comma contraction and the distinction from the source assertion. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical lemma.
